slot.brief: A rod fixed between rigid walls is heated through a known ΔT; find compressive thermal stress using Y and α, possibly combined with a rise in temperature at which stress equals breaking stress.

stem: A rod of cross-sectional area $2.0\ \text{cm}^2$ is stress-free at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and held between rigid walls. It is heated to $30^\circ\text{C}$. Given $Y=2.0\times10^{11}\ \text{Pa}$, $\alpha=1.2\times10^{-5}\ \text{K}^{-1}$ and breaking load $24\ \text{kN}$, what further rise in temperature will just break it? Assume it remains elastic up to breaking.

verdicts.working: Breaking stress = 24,000/(2.0×10⁻⁴) = 1.2×10⁸ Pa. The total rise from 20°C to breaking is σ/(Yα) = 50°C. Since it has already risen 10°C, the further rise is 40°C.

working:
$A=2.0\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2$; $\sigma_b=2.4\times10^4/A=1.2\times10^8\ \text{Pa}$; $\Delta T_b=\sigma_b/(Y\alpha)=50\ \text{K}$; further rise $=50-10=40^\circ\text{C}$.

Independent check: Breaking stress = 24,000/(2.0×10⁻⁴) = 1.2×10⁸ Pa. The total rise from 20°C to breaking is σ/(Yα) = 50°C. Since it has already risen 10°C, the further rise is 40°C.
solution:
For a rod held between rigid walls, thermal stress is $\sigma=Y\alpha\Delta T$. The breaking stress is $\sigma_b=\dfrac{24\times10^3}{2.0\times10^{-4}}=1.2\times10^8\,\text{Pa}$.
$$\Delta T_b=\frac{\sigma_b}{Y\alpha}=50\,\text{K}$$
It has already risen by $10^\circ\text{C}$, so the further rise is $50-10=40^\circ\text{C}$.
